lede: THE WATERS OF GIVERNY ARE HERE - To think painting and to produce an object. In an overflight over the history of art, a landing on the water.
about.0:
THE WATERS OF GIVERNY ARE HERE - To think painting and to produce an object. In
an overflight over the history of art, a landing on the water. Not that solid water,
fruit of the trap/trompe l’œil, but that other one, pure evanescence that dances
before the eyes, from the impressionist adventure onward, pure abstraction. The equation/
resulting work, H2O Monet, sets out to define a three-dimensional space geometrically inscribed on the support, where the experience of the eye with water must take
place within the spatial circumscription, performing the “magic” of light and shadow, its projection
that provokes the visual impression of water.
Marília Panitz, extract from the book Instalações Barja - 2005, p. 8; text “Ao que importa uma
resposta”.
trecho.0: Far from considering that Wagner Barja’s poetics falls outside visual poetry, a large part of his works must be inscribed within its coordinates of expanded seeing. Above all those in which nomenclature forms part of the work: his naming plays a determinant role, in a triangle of verbal, conceptual and visual powers. There are several works, then, that come to function with the verbal-visual element activated, generating a plural field of aesthetic forces in which even the territory of sensoriality is produced by conceptual and reflexive contiguity. Thus the set of Da², H2O Monet, Fike and even Natureza X Cultura = Barbárie draws near. In them, the submerged conversation that is established and aims at a certain infinitude, in a writing (“this insane game of writing”, as Blanchot would say), which here also bets on a simultaneity of language. The very idea of “Obranome”, (motive of curatorship and work), lies in that non-reductionist frequency.
